name: Yule
date_note: Around December 21 (the winter solstice), often extended through the twelve days of Christmas.
history: Yule is linked to Germanic and Norse midwinter festivals. Historic practices include burning a Yule log, and wassailing, which meant drinking a spiced hot drink and blessing the orchards. Wassail was a mulled drink of ale or cider with roasted apples and spices. Many Yule foods are shared with later Christmas customs.
confidence: The Yule log and wassail are documented in later sources. Their earliest pagan roots are debated.

dishes.name: Wassail (spiced hot cider)
dishes.ritual_note: Wassail was shared around the fire. Pour a cup for each person and offer a wish for the new year.
ingredients: Optional: 500 ml ale, added at the end
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C. Roast the apple halves cut-side up for 20 minutes, until soft.
Put the cider, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, nutmeg and sugar in a pan. Simmer gently for 15 minutes. Do not boil.
Add the roasted apples to the pan and keep warm on low heat.
If using ale, stir it in just before serving so it stays lively.
dishes.safety: Leave out the ale for a non-alcoholic version. Serve warm, not boiling.

dishes.name: Gingerbread loaf
dishes.ritual_note: Spiced cakes and loaves were common midwinter foods. Cut a slice for each guest.
steps: Heat the oven to 170 C (150 C fan). Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Sift the flour, spices and bicarbonate of soda into a bowl.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy. Beat in the treacle and the egg.
Fold in the dry ingredients, then the warm milk, until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then on a rack.
dishes.safety: Keeps for up to 5 days wrapped in foil.
